Spreading Probability Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch64.R
centrality_spreading_probability.Rd

Spreading probability centrality (SP; Bao et al. 2017) sums, over the nodes within a radius of a node, the number of shortest paths to each, discounted by the mean degree of the network once per step: $$SP(i) = \sum_{j:\,1 \le d_{ij} \le r} \sigma_{ij} \langle k \rangle^{-d_{ij}},$$ with \(\sigma_{ij}\) the number of shortest paths between \(i\) and \(j\), \(d_{ij}\) their distance and \(\langle k \rangle\) the mean degree. The reciprocal of the mean degree stands for the probability that an infection crosses one tie.

Usage

centrality_spreading_probability(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses sp_radius (the largest distance summed over, default 3).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. sp_radius is 3 by default, the value the source uses; Inf sums over every node that can be reached. With sp_radius = 1 the score is the degree divided by the mean degree. The node itself is not counted. Isolated nodes score 0, and so does every node of a network without ties. The source prints no value of the measure on a small network, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. A sp_radius that is neither a whole number of at least one nor Inf raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Bao, Z.-K., Ma, C., Xiang, B.-B. and Zhang, H.-F. (2017). Identification of influential nodes in complex networks: Method from spreading probability viewpoint. Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications, 468, 391-397. doi:10.1016/j.physa.2016.10.086 .

See also

centrality_kpath, centrality_semilocal, centrality.

Examples

centrality_spreading_probability(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   1.337449   1.522634   1.570645   1.625514   1.440329   1.440329   1.220850 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   1.440329   1.488340   1.371742 
centrality_spreading_probability(regulation_net, sp_radius = 2)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   1.337449   1.522634   1.570645   1.625514   1.440329   1.440329   1.220850 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   1.440329   1.488340   1.371742
